1) the dimeric protein form is required for ligand binding in many cases; 2) the presence of a covalently bound ligand in the protein preparation has to be taken into consideration; 3) the apo-protein can be obtained by denaturation/refolding of the purified protein.
(1) the dimeric LBDs are the preferred target for screening; and (2) the apo-LBDs have to be used in the screening.

(1) differential scanning fluorimetric protein screening of commercial compound collections is a powerful tool to identify the signal molecule of sensor proteins; (2) the dimeric protein form needs to be used for the screening; (3) the apo-form of the protein needs to be generated by denaturing and subsequent refolding for the identification of ligand molecules.
